generation_fit: The board is fictional/symbolic UI art and does not depict a real person, place, event, or archival object. ImageGen is the approved source mode for an illustrated background panel.

reference_input.role: existing project source used as layout/style reference only

canonical_reference.note: The canonical vanilla_reference library has no dedicated scripted-GUI or UI-panel family. The existing project source was the primary layout reference; the nearest HOI4 report-art contact sheet was consulted only for restrained period palette and surface treatment.

prompt_summary: Front-facing HOI4-style painted 1930s-1940s metal-and-wood Muster Board: header plaque, top metric/tab band, six left dossier wells, central overview/formation lots/requests/history zones, right registry-command well for claimant/command/anomalous surfaces, and lower action band; army marks, field maps, seals, brass fasteners, and restrained geometric anomaly motifs; no people, portraits, buttons, readable words, pseudo-text, watermark, modern props, or important detail under the future close button.

visual_notes: Six distinct stacked left-rail wells are readable at the target canvas.
Central board has four intentional sub-zones: map-like overview, formation-lot grid, request list surface, and anomaly/history surface.
Right-side registry/command well contains a map plate, seal slots, document stack, and filing pocket for claimant, command, and anomalous overlays.
Header plaque, top metric/tab band, and lower action band leave clear overlay-safe surfaces.
No humans, portraits, readable generated words, pseudo-text, modern props, or UI buttons appear in the runtime art.
Important decoration is kept away from the future close-button area in the upper-right.

remaining_risks: Main agent must verify the existing GUI's content rectangles and close-button placement against this art at runtime scale.
Main agent owns .gfx/.gui wiring and should keep the provided sprite name and stable DDS path unchanged.
